source: Built by tools/build-surface-maps.sh from public-domain data. Moon: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, CGI Moon Kit (https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4720/); colour from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera wide-angle mosaic, elevation from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter gridded data averaged from 16 to 8 pixels per degree. Mars: USGS Astrogeology Science Center; colour from the Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic (232 m), elevation from the Mars Global Surveyor MOLA mosaic (463 m), both reduced by nearest neighbour. Earth: colour from NASA Blue Marble Next Generation, cloud-free (NASA GIBS, https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov); elevation and ocean depth from NOAA NCEI ETOPO 2022 at one arc-minute (doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74) averaged to 8 pixels per degree.
units: Paths are relative to the site root. Both maps are equirectangular with the north pole at the top and longitude 0 at the centre. Heights are raw little-endian signed 16-bit metres relative to reference_radius_m, height_width by height_height samples. albedo_gain is a dimensionless display choice: it scales the stretched mosaic back toward the body's true reflectance.
